Synopsis:
    Energy infrastructure faces a growing wave of AI-enhanced cyberattacks from state-aligned hacking groups (Russia, Iran, China). AI is lowering the barrier to entry for attackers by automating attack paths, enabling protocol-level exploits against operational technology, and accelerating vulnerability identification. Smaller utilities and renewable energy assets are the most exposed due to budget constraints and legacy/internet-connected equipment. Defensive recommendations include asset inventories, SANS ICS Critical Controls, AI-assisted patching, and standardized cybersecurity blueprints. The asymmetry between attackers (need to succeed once) and defenders (must succeed always) remains the core structural challenge.
